questions.question: What is the structural relationship between butane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃) and isobutane [(CH₃)₂CHCH₃]?

options.label: A
options.text: Enantiomers.

options.label: B
options.text: Conformational rotamers.

options.label: C
options.text: Constitutional (structural) isomers: identical molecular formula (C₄H₁₀) with completely different atom connectivity.

options.label: D
options.text: Diastereomers.

questions.correct_answer: Constitutional (structural) isomers: identical molecular formula (C₄H₁₀) with completely different atom connectivity.
questions.explanation: Constitutional isomers share the same molecular formula but have different atom connectivity.

questions.question: How do stereoisomers differ fundamentally from constitutional isomers?

options.label: A
options.text: Stereoisomers have different numbers of carbon atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Stereoisomers have different functional groups.

options.label: C
options.text: Stereoisomers possess identical molecular formulas AND identical atom connectivity, differing only in the 3D spatial orientation of their bonds.

options.label: D
options.text: Stereoisomers cannot be isolated.

questions.correct_answer: Stereoisomers possess identical molecular formulas AND identical atom connectivity, differing only in the 3D spatial orientation of their bonds.
questions.explanation: Stereoisomers share identical IUPAC connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms (e.g., cis/trans, R/S).

questions.question: When evaluating the relative stability of resonance contributors, which rule takes top priority?

options.label: A
options.text: Structures with maximum formal charge separation are preferred.

options.label: B
options.text: Structures with fewer single bonds are preferred.

options.label: C
options.text: Structures where every atom satisfies the octet rule (full valence shell) are vastly more significant than structures with open octets.

options.label: D
options.text: Structures with positive charge on electronegative atoms are preferred.

questions.correct_answer: Structures where every atom satisfies the octet rule (full valence shell) are vastly more significant than structures with open octets.
questions.explanation: Octet satisfaction is the foremost criterion for resonance stability, overriding electronegativity rules.

questions.topic: Major vs Minor Resonance Hybrid Contributor
questions.question: In the resonance contributors of formaldehyde [H₂C=O ↔ H₂C⁺-O⁻], which contributor is major?

options.label: A
options.text: The zwitterionic structure H₂C⁺-O⁻ is major.

options.label: B
options.text: The neutral structure H₂C=O is major because all atoms satisfy the octet rule with zero formal charge separation.

options.label: C
options.text: Both contributors contribute exactly 50%.

options.label: D
options.text: Neither structure exists.

questions.correct_answer: The neutral structure H₂C=O is major because all atoms satisfy the octet rule with zero formal charge separation.
questions.explanation: Neutral contributors with complete octets and minimal charge separation dominate the resonance hybrid.

questions.question: When a curved arrow moves a lone pair from oxygen to form a new C=O π bond, what happens to the formal charge on oxygen?

options.label: A
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen remains unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen decreases by -1.

options.label: C
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen increases by +1 (e.g., -1 becomes 0, or 0 becomes +1).

options.label: D
options.text: The formal charge doubles.

questions.correct_answer: The formal charge on oxygen increases by +1 (e.g., -1 becomes 0, or 0 becomes +1).
questions.explanation: Donating a lone pair to form a shared bond reduces nonbonding electron count by 2 and adds 1 shared electron, increasing formal charge by +1.

questions.question: Why is the nitrogen lone pair in acetamide (CH₃CONH₂) delocalized whereas in ethylamine (CH₃CH₂NH₂) it is localized?

options.label: A
options.text: The nitrogen in acetamide is sp³ hybridized.

options.label: B
options.text: Acetamide has no hydrogen atoms on nitrogen.

options.label: C
options.text: In acetamide, the nitrogen lone pair resides in an unhybridized 2p orbital that overlaps with the adjacent carbonyl C=O π system.

options.label: D
options.text: Ethylamine contains an aromatic ring.

questions.correct_answer: In acetamide, the nitrogen lone pair resides in an unhybridized 2p orbital that overlaps with the adjacent carbonyl C=O π system.
questions.explanation: Lone pairs adjacent to π systems rehybridize from sp³ to 2p to participate in stabilizing resonance delocalization.

questions.question: What does the true resonance hybrid structure of the acetaldehyde enolate [CH₂=CH-O⁻] look like?

options.label: A
options.text: A cyclic three-membered ring.

options.label: B
options.text: A continuous 3-center 4π electron system with partial negative charges on both the α-carbon (δ-) and oxygen (δ-), with greatest charge on oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: A localized carbanion with no charge on oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: A symmetrical neutral alkene.

questions.correct_answer: A continuous 3-center 4π electron system with partial negative charges on both the α-carbon (δ-) and oxygen (δ-), with greatest charge on oxygen.
questions.explanation: The resonance hybrid has partial double-bond character across C-C and C-O, with negative charge shared between C and O (predominantly on electronegative O).

questions.question: Why do cis-2-butene and trans-2-butene exist as distinct, isolable stereoisomers at room temperature?

options.label: A
options.text: Restricted rotation around the carbon-carbon double bond due to the ~260 kJ/mol π bond energy barrier prevents spontaneous interconversion.

options.label: B
options.text: They are enantiomers that rotate polarized light in opposite directions.

options.label: C
options.text: They interconvert at 10¹² times per second.

options.label: D
options.text: They have different molecular formulas.

questions.correct_answer: Restricted rotation around the carbon-carbon double bond due to the ~260 kJ/mol π bond energy barrier prevents spontaneous interconversion.
questions.explanation: The carbon-carbon π bond prevents free rotation, locking substituents in distinct spatial orientations (cis vs trans).

questions.question: Why does cis-1,2-dichloroethene possess a large molecular dipole moment (1.90 D) while trans-1,2-dichloroethene has zero dipole moment?

options.label: A
options.text: The cis isomer is an ionic salt.

options.label: B
options.text: The cis isomer contains more chlorine atoms than the trans isomer.

options.label: C
options.text: In the cis isomer, the two polar C-Cl bond dipoles point in the same direction and reinforce; in the trans isomer, they point in opposite directions and cancel exactly.

options.label: D
options.text: The trans isomer is nonplanar.

questions.correct_answer: In the cis isomer, the two polar C-Cl bond dipoles point in the same direction and reinforce; in the trans isomer, they point in opposite directions and cancel exactly.
questions.explanation: Vector cancellation of equal and opposite C-Cl dipoles in the centrosymmetric trans isomer yields a zero molecular dipole moment.

questions.question: What is the experimental structural evidence that benzene does not exist as alternating single and double bonds?

options.label: A
options.text: Benzene decomposes instantly in air.

options.label: B
options.text: Benzene has three long bonds and three short bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: All six carbon-carbon bonds have an identical intermediate length of 1.39 Å (between C-C single 1.54 Å and C=C double 1.34 Å) in a regular planar hexagon.

options.label: D
options.text: Benzene is a nonplanar puckered ring.

questions.correct_answer: All six carbon-carbon bonds have an identical intermediate length of 1.39 Å (between C-C single 1.54 Å and C=C double 1.34 Å) in a regular planar hexagon.
questions.explanation: X-ray crystallography reveals identical 1.39 Å bond lengths and 120° angles, confirming completely delocalized 6π aromatic resonance.

questions.question: When a curved arrow moves a lone pair from oxygen to form a new C=O π bond, what happens to the formal charge on oxygen?

options.label: A
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen remains unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: The formal charge doubles.

options.label: C
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen increases by +1 (e.g., -1 becomes 0, or 0 becomes +1).

options.label: D
options.text: The formal charge on oxygen decreases by -1.

questions.correct_answer: The formal charge on oxygen increases by +1 (e.g., -1 becomes 0, or 0 becomes +1).
questions.explanation: Donating a lone pair to form a shared bond reduces nonbonding electron count by 2 and adds 1 shared electron, increasing formal charge by +1.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: In acetamide, the nitrogen lone pair resides in an unhybridized 2p orbital that overlaps with the adjacent carbonyl C=O π system.

questions.question: Why does cis-1,2-dichloroethene possess a large molecular dipole moment (1.90 D) while trans-1,2-dichloroethene has zero dipole moment?

options.label: A
options.text: In the cis isomer, the two polar C-Cl bond dipoles point in the same direction and reinforce; in the trans isomer, they point in opposite directions and cancel exactly.

options.label: B
options.text: The trans isomer is nonplanar.

options.label: C
options.text: The cis isomer contains more chlorine atoms than the trans isomer.

options.label: D
options.text: The cis isomer is an ionic salt.

questions.correct_answer: In the cis isomer, the two polar C-Cl bond dipoles point in the same direction and reinforce; in the trans isomer, they point in opposite directions and cancel exactly.
questions.explanation: Vector cancellation of equal and opposite C-Cl dipoles in the centrosymmetric trans isomer yields a zero molecular dipole moment.

questions.question: What is the experimental structural evidence that benzene does not exist as alternating single and double bonds?

options.label: A
options.text: All six carbon-carbon bonds have an identical intermediate length of 1.39 Å (between C-C single 1.54 Å and C=C double 1.34 Å) in a regular planar hexagon.

options.label: B
options.text: Benzene has three long bonds and three short bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: Benzene decomposes instantly in air.

options.label: D
options.text: Benzene is a nonplanar puckered ring.

questions.correct_answer: All six carbon-carbon bonds have an identical intermediate length of 1.39 Å (between C-C single 1.54 Å and C=C double 1.34 Å) in a regular planar hexagon.
questions.explanation: X-ray crystallography reveals identical 1.39 Å bond lengths and 120° angles, confirming completely delocalized 6π aromatic resonance.

questions.question: What is the structural relationship between butane (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃) and isobutane [(CH₃)₂CHCH₃]?

options.label: A
options.text: Diastereomers.

options.label: B
options.text: Conformational rotamers.

options.label: C
options.text: Enantiomers.

options.text: Constitutional (structural) isomers: identical molecular formula (C₄H₁₀) with completely different atom connectivity.

questions.correct_answer: Constitutional (structural) isomers: identical molecular formula (C₄H₁₀) with completely different atom connectivity.
questions.explanation: Constitutional isomers share the same molecular formula but have different atom connectivity.

questions.question: How do stereoisomers differ fundamentally from constitutional isomers?

options.label: A
options.text: Stereoisomers possess identical molecular formulas AND identical atom connectivity, differing only in the 3D spatial orientation of their bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Stereoisomers possess identical molecular formulas AND identical atom connectivity, differing only in the 3D spatial orientation of their bonds.
questions.explanation: Stereoisomers share identical IUPAC connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms (e.g., cis/trans, R/S).

questions.question: When evaluating the relative stability of resonance contributors, which rule takes top priority?

options.label: A
options.text: Structures with positive charge on electronegative atoms are preferred.

options.label: B
options.text: Structures where every atom satisfies the octet rule (full valence shell) are vastly more significant than structures with open octets.

options.label: C
options.text: Structures with fewer single bonds are preferred.

options.label: D
options.text: Structures with maximum formal charge separation are preferred.

questions.correct_answer: Structures where every atom satisfies the octet rule (full valence shell) are vastly more significant than structures with open octets.
questions.explanation: Octet satisfaction is the foremost criterion for resonance stability, overriding electronegativity rules.

questions.question: Why do cis-2-butene and trans-2-butene exist as distinct, isolable stereoisomers at room temperature?

questions.explanation: The carbon-carbon π bond prevents free rotation, locking substituents in distinct spatial orientations (cis vs trans).
